task.description: Validate src/design/gh520-backoff-schedule-deterministic-assertion.md, a Type E design fixing GH #520 / ISS-0186's flaky TC-EXP-301-05 test. The design replaces a two-separate-database-round-trip wall-clock delta measurement with a single combined query issued once immediately after Queue.markRetry returns, reading attempt_count, status, next_attempt_at, and NOW() in one statement execution, tightening the tolerance from +/-500ms to +/-50ms. Verify: (1) the tolerance justification is sound -- the design claims +/-50ms accounts for same-connection statement-dispatch latency between the UPDATE (inside markRetry) and the follow-up SELECT, and explicitly does NOT claim 0ms is safe because the two statements are not in the same transaction (so PostgreSQL's per-transaction NOW() stability doesn't apply across them) -- confirm this reasoning is technically correct against actual PostgreSQL semantics (check whether markRetry's UPDATE and the test's follow-up SELECT really do run as separate statements/transactions, or whether they could be combined further); (2) the assertion remains non-tautological -- it must still fail if markRetry's backoff interval computation regresses; (3) all four expected_backoff values (5000/30000/120000/600000ms) are still exercised; (4) no production code is touched. RE-CHECK: CODE-DESIGNER reworked the design after your BLOCKER finding -- corrected the transaction-semantics analysis (confirmed both markRetry and the follow-up SELECT run inside the same TestHarness-opened transaction, so NOW() is frozen and identical for both), re-derived the tolerance from 50ms to 1.0ms (pure client-side float round-trip epsilon), and reconciled why the ORIGINAL two-read test was ever flaky despite NOW() being frozen (the old delta reduced to a pure interval difference with no wall-clock component at all -- the real defect was a comparison-correctness gap, not timing jitter). Re-validate from scratch, including independently re-deriving the reconciliation argument -- do not just accept it because it sounds plausible.
acceptance_criteria: The +/-50ms tolerance justification is verified against actual PostgreSQL statement/transaction semantics, not just trusted
The assertion remains non-tautological and still exercises all 4 expected_backoff values

result.summary: Re-validated reworked src/design/gh520-backoff-schedule-deterministic-assertion.md after rework 1/3. Independently re-verified transaction-semantics claim against tests/integration/helpers.zig:1085 (TestHarness.init single conn.begin(), never committed) and vendor/pg/pg.zig:149-190 (exec/query issue no implicit BEGIN/COMMIT; only begin/commit/rollback touch tx state) -- confirmed all statements in TC-EXP-301-05 run in one transaction, so NOW() is frozen and identical for markRetry and the read-back. Independently re-derived the reconciliation algebra from the current test source (tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig:570-696): next_ms_after - next_ms_before reduces to interval_after - interval_before with frozen_NOW cancelling exactly, confirming zero wall-clock component. Verified via git history (git diff 60fae79 HEAD) that TC-EXP-301-05 has been byte-identical since the ISS-0158 fix commit, i.e. the code ISS-0186 was filed against IS this same single-transaction test -- there is no separate-connection prior version, so the reconciliation is not inventing a convenient discrepancy. The design correctly names the actual flake mechanism as execution-order/state dependence in what the seed loop last wrote, not clock jitter, resolving the apparent contradiction with ISS-0186's original jitter theory. 1.0ms tolerance confirmed as pure float round-trip epsilon (5000x headroom vs smallest expected_backoff=5000ms). Assertion remains non-tautological (4 distinct backoff values, bound comparison retained). No production code touched (queue.zig unmodified, explicitly out of scope). lint_design_artefact.py exits 0, no BLOCKER/MAJOR.
